purpose: Review the Darwin Initiative 24-016 Year 1 report for the earliest public Cagayan River Basin janitor-fish lead, and separate community monitoring statements from specimen-verified occurrences.

source.title: Darwin Initiative Annual Report, project 24-016: Sustainable Community-Based Stewardship of Freshwater Resources in Northern Philippines
source.provider: Zoological Society of London; Darwin Initiative; project partners DA-BFAR Region II and DENR Region II
source.license: No item-specific open reuse license was identified in the reviewed report.

reviewedEvidence.monitoringMethod: The report says invasive-species data collection was integrated into community monitoring group FID collection across 12 freshwater sanctuaries and was being collected on a bi-weekly basis. It also explicitly reports data-collection issues at some sites that were still being addressed.
reviewedEvidence.municipalityLeads: During site visits, discussions with community monitoring group members indicated janitor fish in Peñablanca, Maddela, and Nagtipunan. The report says local fisheries evidence was anecdotal and suggested the fish may have been in the region for some time. No exact river/lake, barangay, collection date, observer record, specimen ID, or accession is provided for these municipality-level statements.
reviewedEvidence.sourceTaxonLabel: The report prints 'Pterygoplichthus pardalis' and associates that name with its janitor-fish lead. Preserve this spelling as quoted source text; the spelling alone does not resolve current taxonomy or prove the identity of a specimen.
reviewedEvidence.annexPhotographs: Annex 13 contains two photographs captioned as the invasive janitor fish. The images are not linked to a named collection locality, date, field event, collector, voucher, or catalogue number in the reviewed report, so they cannot validate any of the three municipality leads.
reviewedEvidence.laterContext: The 2021 BFAR Region II annual report separately reports 2 kg of janitor fish retrieved in Nagtipunan, but it does not name a waterbody or link that catch to a scientific identity. The two reports are compatible as a lead but do not provide a specimen crosswalk or independent event-level dataset.

qualityAndReuseLimits: The 2018 claim is based on community discussions and anecdotal local fisheries evidence; it is not a voucher-backed survey record.
The reported FID programme had known data-collection problems, and the public annual report does not provide the underlying monitoring list or event records.
The report's municipality-level lead does not justify assigning the fish to a specific waterbody, sanctuary, coordinate, or current range polygon.
The source's spelling 'Pterygoplichthus pardalis' must not be silently changed or accepted as a canonical identification without specimen-based taxonomic review.
The Annex 13 photographs lack locality and specimen metadata and are not copied or used as identification evidence.
No item-specific reuse license was verified. No species/occurrence rows, coordinates, geometry, invasive-status claims, safety/legal advice, or app content are approved from this report.
nextAction: Search non-government university and journal repositories for a specimen-backed northern Luzon loricariid record or a public copy of the project CMG/FID dataset, checking whether a source provides dated, named-waterbody observations. Keep the three localities as research leads until identity and site precision are independently verified.
